criteria.evidence: The BFF now takes the address the platform's trusted proxy appended (web/server/utils/clientAddress.ts), not the leftmost X-Forwarded-For element, and the server no longer exempts a loopback address. web/tests/client-address.test.ts covers six cases: a spoofed leading element is ignored, two trusted hops skip the proxies' own entries, a missing or too short header falls back to the socket address, a non-address value is not forwarded at all, a corrupted hop count falls back to one proxy instead of trusting the client header, and the setting stays in the private runtime config. server/tests/rate-limits.test.ts asserts that a loopback address forwarded by a trusted BFF hits the auth.verify.ip threshold like any other client bucket, both with the plugin's own forwarded flag and with the real request-tracing signature. web/tests/e2e/125-rate-limit-bypass.spec.ts drives the live stack: ten verifyMagicLink calls carrying X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1 pass and the eleventh answers RATE_LIMITED with a positive retryAfter. RED confirmed: with the loopback exemption restored that scenario fails (no RATE_LIMITED). CI run 36283108045 on the tested SHA.

rootFieldCounts counts every occurrence of a root field, including aliases and repeated fragment spreads, and the plugin sums the cost per bucket and enforces it once. server/tests/rate-limits.test.ts: a single document with 20 aliases of requestMagicLink consumes the whole auth.link.ip window, the store is consulted exactly once with cost 20, and the next single request is RATE_LIMITED; a document with limit+1 aliases is rejected whole and the resolver is never called; rootFieldCounts returns { requestMagicLink: 3, verifyMagicLink: 1 } for a batch and counts a fragment spread named twice plus an inline fragment as three calls. Cost is carried through both stores: database (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE adding the cost, expired window restarting at the cost) and Redis (one INCRBY, window opened when the count equals the cost), each with unit tests and a real-PostgreSQL case. web/tests/e2e/125-rate-limit-bypass.spec.ts: a document with 11 aliases of verifyMagicLink answers RATE_LIMITED with null data. RED confirmed: with unique-name deduplication that scenario fails. CI run 36283108045 on the tested SHA.

The address-based exemption is gone; the §3 system calls never reach this middleware, and that is now asserted instead of assumed. server/tests/rate-limits.test.ts, describe 'исключения §3': a real http server built as withHealth(yoga-with-the-rate-limit-plugin) answers 15 pairs of GET /health and GET / (the platform port probe) without consulting the counter store at all, while an ordinary GraphQL POST from the same loopback address consumes the bucket once; a third case reads every source file of server/src/jobs and requires no fetch( call and no http(s) URL, so the worker cannot pass through this middleware. No provider webhook exists in the schema yet; when it appears it needs a signature check, not a loopback address.
